pr_comments: Silencing a warning does not fix the issue. If you see this in the log, something goes wrong and should be fixed. Instead of hiding the symptom you should investigate the root cause.

@FernetMenta  Do you have an idea of what goes wrong? From reading, the first WARNING (in player) infact was not correct as it did not have PAUSE state in mind where no new frames come from decoder. But here I don't get why it's triggered as the current frame should just be painted again, right?

> @FernetMenta Do you have an idea of what goes wrong? From reading, the first WARNING (in player) infact was not correct as it did not have PAUSE state in mind where no new frames come from decoder. But here I don't get why it's triggered as the current frame should just be painted again, right?

Paused state is not relevant here. When paused VPV submits the same frame continuously to renderer and renderer should provide free buffers for it.
Seems nothing is delivered. Which is why we timeout here and spam?
Sorry, I was wrong. Meanwhile RM has access to the clock and pause state does matter. I think this PR is ok as is.

Hello, I apologize for not seeing this in time to ask a question about it, but I was wondering if you think it would be beneficial to add to this to also suppress the message if the Video stream is in a stalled state:

```
    if (m_speed != DVD_PLAYSPEED_PAUSE && !m_stalled)
      CLog::Log(LOGWARNING, "{} - timeout waiting for buffer", __FUNCTION__);
```

A secondary concern with Issues [18389](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/issues/18389) and [17041](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/issues/17041) that was not resolved with PR [19048](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/pull/19048) is the "timeout waiting for buffer" logspam condition.  I made no attempt to address this since it wasn't related to the main playback issue.

Q: If the video stream is stalled, is it acceptable to suppress this message?

Commenting on a merged PR is absolutely bad form, and I apologize for that, but I didn't want to write up a PR for something that's conceptually incorrect (again).
Based on lack of feedback I intend to issue a PR to address this as time allows; I do not see any reason for this log message to exist if the underlying video stream is in a known "stalled" state.

comments: This problem still exists in Beta2, anyone looking at this?
@Montellese maybe something like https://github.com/gabime/spdlog/issues/696 could be implemented to avoid this and similar issues?
@enen92 This is not about repeated messages, the issue here is pausing a video should not cause any "Warning" messages to start with

@enen92 while your idea would mitigate the issue and will restore the previous logging behaviour I have to agree with @Gujal00.

But in case you want to integrate the `dup_filter_sink` anyway there are two places it can go:
* if it should apply only to the logs being written to the log file it should be placed "around" `CLog::m_fileSink` as a `dup_filter_sink_mt`.
* if it should apply to all log outputs (including platform specific debug logs) we could change the initialization of `CLog::m_sinks` from `m_sinks(std::make_shared<spdlog::sinks::dist_sink_mt>())` to something like `m_sinks(std::make_shared<spdlog::sinks::dup_filter_sink_mt>(std::chrono::seconds(10)))`.

Thanks for the tips Montellese, and glad you're feeling well again :)
My comment was not an attempt to swipe this or similar issues under the bed but to know exactly if (and where) such a "feature" could be implemented. There are certainly legit cases for repeated log messages in a short period of time and we have a lot of bug reports regarding the log size. Filtering similar messages could at least help with that.
Thanks

Problem still persisting on the RC1 release.
Would be great if someone looks at this before final release
Please see #19082 for a generic solution to the logging problem since we moved to `spdlog`.

review_comments:
I wonder if this could be kept. Now when the other side (e.g. the player user) says OUTPUT_AGAIN, it should receive something or better present the last buffer once more. (Why keeping: if we are not paused, but really render is stuck, then we would not see it anymore. But I admit I don't have a better idea at hand.

Btw. do you still see a 100% CPU usage when this block is hit?

If we keep that log here, it will keep spamming. I guess introducing a new parameter for this would be a hack?
As for cpu usage: I see no real difference between play and pause state. Both are ~50% CPU

The key thing here is that the RenderManager should have no idea about player's internal state. Changing the interface of rendermanager to introduce something like: Pause() though would work.

Never the less out of scope of this PR. We could make a it a LOGDEBUG, then at least if someone wants to debug these things they'd see it and normal users won't?
